evidence: Receiving online DO at decision time t=52.0 h = 11.04 mg/L (receiving_observations, simulated_online_sensor).
Receiving DO minimum over observed history ~8.86 mg/L (feed transient around t=23-27 h), all >2 mg/L.
Source-1 DO minimum over remaining-horizon analog (t~60-96 h) ~7.44 mg/L; source-2 ~8.2, source-3 ~8.1 mg/L.
Aligned-time offset receiving vs source ~1.5-2 mg/L (e.g., t=52 h: source 12.8 mg/L vs receiving 11.0 mg/L), giving projected receiving minimum ~5.5-6.5 mg/L under KEEP.
Delayed P assays (receiving: 0.023 g/L at t=59 sample, 0.924 at t=179, 2.74 at t=239) show growth on track, comparable to source batches at aligned times, so no corrective intervention is indicated.
args.rationale: KEEP is the supported feasible plan. The receiving DO trajectory is observed online and currently at 11.04 mg/L at t=52 h, with a historical minimum of ~8.86 mg/L during the sharpest observed feed-demand transient. Source batches, which show the same feed-event dynamics, bottom out at 7.4-8.3 mg/L over the analogous remaining horizon (t~60-96 h); the receiving process runs ~1.5-2 mg/L below source at aligned times, so a source-calibrated worst-case projection gives a receiving minimum of ~5.5-6.5 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L hard DO limit. Feed reductions (reduce_feed, strong_feed_reduction) would cut product mass with no constraint benefit, and increase_air/combined add no needed margin. This appears to be a normal, stable case requiring no intervention.
args.uncertainty: The projection relies on source-calibrated dynamics applied to the receiving process, which differ (hidden parameters/states). If the receiving run has a larger upcoming oxygen demand than any source batch showed, the dip could be deeper; however, the margin (~3.5-4.5 mg/L above the limit even under the pessimistic offset-adjusted estimate) and the directly observed, well-behaved online DO trace make a constraint violation under KEEP unlikely. Assay timing (20 h delay) means the delayed product data reflect conditions up to t=32 h only; this does not change the DO-based conclusion.
